articles.title: Human — Arcane-Receptive
articles.summary: Humans possess unusually plastic physical, mental, social, and magical development, a quality often called Adaptable Potential. Rather than expressing one strongly specialized inherited form, human potential responds exceptionally well to environment, experience, training, hardship, and opportunity. This selection describes how that potential developed before play; it is not a human subspecies, ethnicity, culture, profession, or personality type. Your mind and body proved unusually receptive to magical development, allowing magical concepts, control exercises, and mana conditioning to take hold readily without determining which Arcana you possess.

articles.title: Dhampir
articles.summary: Dhampirs are living mortals with partial vampiric ancestry or a stable vampire-touched bloodline. They may have cool skin, subtle fangs, unusual eyes, muted pulse, and pronounced nocturnal senses, but they are not Vampires and do not automatically possess the Beast, blood dependence, immortality, sunlight burning, invitation restrictions, missing reflections, or the Vampire subsystem.

articles.title: Dragonfolk
articles.summary: Dragonfolk are full-sized draconic humanoids with scaled bodies, distinctly draconic faces, horns, claws, tails, and powerful humanoid builds. They are mortal people rather than lesser dragons and can use ordinary humanoid clothing, armor, weapons, and equipment with practical adjustments for their horns and tails. Wings, breath weapons, and supernatural elemental powers are not universal Dragonfolk traits.

articles.title: Dragonkin
articles.summary: Dragonkin look fundamentally human but carry prominent draconic traits. They retain a fully humanlike face, skin, hands, feet, legs, and body plan while normally possessing horns, a scaled tail, and draconic wings, sometimes accompanied by slit pupils or small scale patches. They are not full humanoid dragons and should never be given reptilian heads, muzzles, full-body scales, digitigrade monster legs, or Dragonfolk anatomy.

articles.title: Dwarf
articles.summary: Dwarves are shorter and broader than humans, with dense builds, strong bones, powerful musculature, and long-lived mortal physiology. Dwarf ancestry does not automatically grant smithing, engineering, mining, weapon training, clan culture, or a mountain upbringing.

articles.title: Elf
articles.summary: Elves are long-lived mortal humanoids with pointed ears, graceful proportions, and naturally keen senses. Their ancestry does not determine culture, profession, morality, magical tradition, or preference for nature; those come from Origin Culture, Upbringing, and lived experience.

articles.title: Gnome
articles.summary: Gnomes are small mortal humanoids with fine hand control, sensitive touch, sharp close attention, and compact bodies suited to precise manipulation. Gnome ancestry does not automatically make someone an engineer, alchemist, scholar, inventor, or mage.

articles.title: Halfling
articles.summary: Halflings are small, resilient mortal humanoids with compact builds, light movement, and proportions that let them pass through crowded or larger-built environments easily. Halfling ancestry does not determine hospitality, cooking, farming, trade, criminality, or any particular culture.

articles.title: Lizardfolk
articles.summary: Lizardfolk are fully reptilian humanoids with scales, reptilian heads and eyes, tails, claws, and strong jaws. Different lineages may resemble monitors, iguanas, crocodilians, geckos, desert lizards, or other reptiles while retaining an upright humanoid body plan compatible with ordinary equipment. Lizardfolk are natural mortal people and have no inherent connection to dragons.

articles.title: Orc
articles.summary: Orcs are large, robust mortal humanoids typically marked by powerful builds, broad features, pronounced tusks or tusk-like teeth, and a physiology capable of sustained physical exertion. Skin tones vary widely by lineage and region. Orcs are a people rather than a warrior profession: culture, upbringing, status, work, faith, and temperament come from their actual lives.

articles.title: Spiritfolk
articles.summary: Spiritfolk are living mortal people whose lineage has been shaped by spirits, old shrines, ancestor pacts, nature forces, local gods, or other persistent contact with the unseen world. Their exact manifestation is intentionally broad and may include luminous eyes, unusual markings, strange hair, omen-like sensations, or a subtle spiritual presence. They are not ghosts, undead, or automatically religious.

They are not angels, chosen servants of a deity, automatically virtuous, or proof of divine favor. Dawnmarked Caelari express that inheritance through radiance, luminous or reflective eyes, bright markings, and an instinctive affinity for light.
